title: Close native-galaxy parity with physical HIP-less observation overlays and parent-owned camera persistence

scope.subject: Native YEIS galaxy observed-host completeness and return-state persistence

research_summary: The native YEIS renderer is viable and committed, but two product-semantic gaps still block default cutover. First, the current NASA bridge exposes 32 observed hosts; 27 have exact HIP鈫扝YG matches and route through native StarPoints, while five HIP-less hosts have no native physical star representation and disappear from the native galaxy. Reusing the old V2 visual coordinates is invalid: comparing 27 HIP-matched hosts against the native HYG positions produced ~24.7 pc median error because V2 uses a deliberately remapped galactic presentation frame. The pinned MIT build-stars.mjs provides the exact authoritative conversion: HYG equatorial pc 鈫?J2000 ecliptic math by -obliquity 鈫?scene (x,z,-y). Recomputing NASA RA/Dec/distance in that frame reduced the matched-host position disagreement to 0.86 pc median; remaining disagreement is catalogue distance/astrometry variance, not a frame error. Therefore store the NASA-derived physical scene-frame position explicitly on observed markers and render only HIP-less hosts as a lightweight native sky overlay; never fuzzy-match names. Second, YeisGalaxyScene currently owns CameraController locally, so entering a system unmounts it and returning recreates the opening view. Preserve only camera position/quaternion in a ref owned by the persistent UniverseCanvas, then restore them when the native galaxy remounts. This reuses the existing native controller and React/R3F lifecycle rather than building a second navigation state system.

sources.finding: The pinned MIT catalogue builder defines the exact HYG equatorial-pc 鈫?ecliptic-J2000 鈫?scene-frame transform used by stars.bin: rotate about x by -23.439291掳, then store scene (x,z,-y).
NASA Exoplanet Archive pscomppars supplies RA, Dec and system distance independently of HIP, so HIP-less confirmed hosts still have sufficient physical coordinates for an explicit overlay.

A ref preserves mutable state across renders without causing rerenders; owning the native camera snapshot in the persistent parent lets an unmounted/remounted scene restore view state without module-global state.
R3F scene components can own imperative Three objects while parent React components retain lifecycle state; this fits a parent view-state ref plus native renderer guest component.

search_ladder.conclusion: The complete YEIS product already solves its own camera lifecycle but importing the whole app would undo the one-shell architecture; parity should be completed inside the current R3F host.
The current R3F host and native CameraController already contain the needed rendering/navigation machinery; only explicit overlay data and parent-owned snapshot state are missing.
Use NASA RA/Dec/distance for HIP-less observed positions, transformed by the exact pinned HYG scene-frame convention. Keep exact HIP identity when available and never substitute fuzzy names.
Use the existing Three Points/BufferGeometry pattern already present in YeisGalaxyScene and a React ref for persistence; no new package or renderer component is required.

coverage_matrix.decision: Use explicit NASA physical coordinates in the authoritative YEIS scene frame.
Overlay preserves the NASA marker identity directly and does not invent a HYG identity.
Follow pinned build-stars transform; reject legacy V2 presentation coordinates.

coverage_matrix.decision: Persist controller position/quaternion in UniverseCanvas-owned ref.

candidates.name: NASA RA/Dec/distance overlay in the exact YEIS/HYG scene frame
candidates.license: NASA public scientific data / archive terms; attribution retained
candidates.reason: Preserves every observed host without fuzzy identity and uses the pinned upstream coordinate convention already authoritative for the native renderer.

candidates.name: Name-match HIP-less NASA hosts to HYG stars
candidates.reason: A display-name similarity must not become astronomical identity authority; false matches are worse than a small explicit overlay.

candidates.name: Reuse existing V2 marker positions directly in native scene
candidates.reason: Measured HIP-matched error (~24.7 pc median) proves the V2 presentation coordinate system is not the native physical scene frame.

candidates.name: Show only HIP-crossmatched observed hosts
candidates.reason: Would silently remove confirmed systems solely because their identity cannot be joined to HYG by HIP.

candidates.name: Persist native camera snapshot in UniverseCanvas-owned React ref
candidates.reason: Preserves native controller position/quaternion across scene unmounts without global state or URL churn and keeps ownership inside the existing React tree.

candidates.name: Store last native camera state in a module singleton
candidates.reason: Works mechanically but leaks view state across component/app instances and makes lifecycle ownership implicit.

candidates.name: Reset native galaxy to the opening overview after every system visit
candidates.reason: Simple and low-coupling, but loses visitor spatial context on every return and therefore fails navigation parity.

candidates.name: Serialize camera position/quaternion into query parameters
candidates.reason: Useful for shareable deep links later, but excessive for simple in-session return persistence and would broaden URL/state semantics unnecessarily.

decision.rationale: Complete native parity with two narrow adapters around already-selected assets: derive HIP-less observed physical positions directly from NASA using the exact pinned YEIS/HYG scene transform, and retain native camera position/quaternion in the persistent R3F parent. This preserves astronomical identity, avoids duplicate render/navigation systems and removes the final known semantic blockers before default cutover.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: It would reduce overlay count but makes name similarity an identity authority, which is globally worse than keeping five explicit confirmed-host points.
Shareable camera URLs are a separate product feature; adding them now would expand the cutover surface for no parity benefit.

decision.fallback: If a HIP-less host lacks finite NASA RA/Dec/distance, omit only that malformed overlay and keep it resolvable from content/search; do not fabricate a HYG match. If camera snapshot restoration fails, keep the native renderer but reset to overview rather than reintroducing V2 camera logic.
